transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Jensen (Redwood AE), Arman Gupta (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM); Nina Patel (Cobalt Platform), Dr. Sunil Mehra (Cobalt ML), Kevin Brooks (Cobalt SecOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check — is now still good?
[00:14] Nina: Yeah good here, thanks. We're just coming out of infra sprint so figured this is a good sync.
[00:31] Maya: Cool. Agenda today: quick onboarding progress, creds and gateway status, bench quick readout, and then fallback/traffic routing plan. Arman will summarize the bench notes.
[00:47] Arman: Hi all, I ran the preliminary perf tests last night on the staging cluster; caveat, this was on a smaller seq len set so numbers will change with longer tokens.
[01:05] Dr. Mehra: When you say smaller, like what distribution? Most of our inference runs are back-and-forth multi-turn, avg 1,200 tokens.
[01:20] Arman: Right, so this first run skewed 128-512. We saw P95 latency ~240ms on the redwood dedi — sorry, Redwood Dedicaed node with 4xA100. There will be differences once we hit your 1,200 tokens.
[01:39] Kevin: Are those numbers with prefix caching? Because our use case will heavily reuse clinical note prefixes.
[01:51] Arman: No, that initial pass didn't enable prefix or KV caching, I wanted a baseline. Next run will enable prefix caching and continuous batching. Expect a meaningful drop in per-token compute for repeated prefixes.
[02:08] Nina: Great. From the onboarding checklist, we've provisioned the VPC peering but the service account for the gateway hasn't been created yet.
[02:21] Maya: Is that a blocker for testing?
[02:26] Nina: For some network-level tests, yes — we can't fully validate egress rules without it.
[02:33] Diego: We can do the bench internally and share logs while you finish service account setup, but full end-to-end will wait on the SA.
[02:45] Maya: Okay let's line up responsibilities in a sec.
[02:51] Speaker 1: quick question on SSO — are we set for SAML or OIDC?
[03:02] Kevin: We prefer SAML for uniformity with our IdP. Also need RBAC scoping so only platform team can call model admin endpoints.
[03:12] Arman: We support SAML; just need the metadata and SP endpoints. Also flag — if you want audit field enrichment (request-id, dataset-tag), we can surface those in logs but we'll need field names from your side.
[03:30] Dr. Mehra: We'll want to capture patient_feed_id and request_context in the token for traceability.
[03:39] Arman: Noted, we'll include that as a logging schema item.
[03:45] Maya: On encryption, you're looking to use your KMS for key management?
[03:50] Kevin: Yes, HSM-backed KMS and we prefer customer-managed keys where possible. Any limitations on on-prem HSM?
[03:58] Arman: Redwood Private supports CMK via KMS and HSM — small caveat on initial setup scripts when mounting HSM in air-gapped. We'll document the steps.
[04:12] Nina: On the network side, do you need a dedicated NAT or will current egress suffice?
[04:18] Diego: For the Dedicated pilot, recommended to have controlled egress — IP allowlist + NAT to restrict outbound. That makes compliance audits nicer.
[04:29] Maya: Okay, bench readout — Arman, can you walk through the test matrix you ran?
[04:35] Arman: Sure. Baseline: 100 concurrent streams, seq 128-512, model xlat-7b (note: model name got mangled in transcript), batching disabled. Metrics: P50 120ms, P95 240ms, token throughput ~1600 tps. Then stress test 300 concurrent small requests; we saw queueing increase and 99th percentile latency jumped to ~1.2s.
[05:02] Dr. Mehra: Does Redwood support automatic fallback to a cheaper variant when capacity hits threshold? Like route to a 3b model?
[05:12] Maya: Yes — routing policies can fallback to a model variant or different region. We can set threshold-based fallbacks and grace degradation.
[05:21] Kevin: We need a deterministic failover, not probabilistic. For audit and billing reasons.
[05:27] Arman: That's doable — we can set strict routing rules: when queue depth > X or p95 > Y, switch to fallback model id and pin it. We'll log the switch event to audit logs.
[05:40] Nina: When that switch happens, will the KV cache be compatible between variants? We rely on a shared prefix cache for context reuse.
[05:49] Arman: Good question. Cache compatibility depends on the model family and tokenizer. If you pick a fallback within the same tokenizer family and quantization profile, we can reuse prefixes; otherwise cache warm-up is needed. We'll outline compatible fallbacks in the doc.
[06:07] Maya: On the credentials timeline, Nina — any ETA for creating the service account?
[06:12] Nina: I can get that done by Monday EOD — 2025-07-28.
[06:18] Maya: Perfect. Once that's in, we'll run the end-to-end bench and run the SAML flow. Also sending the updated security pack includes a network diagram and KMS notes.
[06:29] Kevin: For audit retention we need logs retained for 7 years for some flows. Is that possible?
[06:34] Diego: Long retention is available as an add-on; we'll include pricing and the retention SLA in the pack.
[06:42] Dr. Mehra: For the bench with long tokens, can we test a sustained 2k token session? We want to see memory growth and KV cache behavior.
[06:51] Arman: Yes — next run will include 2k token sequences, prefix caching on, and also an experiment toggling quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit) to understand perf/cost tradeoffs.
[07:04] Maya: Quick question from sales side: any changes to timelines from your procurement side?
[07:10] Nina: Procurement loop is open; security review happens next week. If the pack covers SOC2 and network, procurement should greenlight.
[07:19] Maya: Good. On canary/rollout — we recommend a narrow traffic percent test during low traffic window. Diego, can you own scheduling with Kevin?
[07:27] Diego: Yes I'll coordinate; propose 2-hour window and checklist for rollback.
[07:32] Kevin: Fine with that, also want a runbook with alerting thresholds.
[07:36] Arman: We'll supply a runbook stub and alert thresholds (p95, error rate, queue depth).
[07:44] Speaker 2: there's a note here about token cost — can you quantify savings from prefix caching?
[07:52] Arman: Rough ballpark — for heavy prefix reuse expect 30-45% token cost reduction at steady state. But depends on reuse ratio and caching TTL.
[08:05] Nina: TTL sizing — how aggressive is the default? We don't want stale context across sessions.
[08:12] Arman: Default is conservative TTL 30 minutes but configurable per route. We can set stricter TTLs for PHI-sensitive flows.
[08:21] Dr. Mehra: PHI handling — are we isolating logs or redaction?
[08:26] Diego: We can route logs to your dedicated log bucket and show PII redaction options. Full redaction is available but we need to map what fields to redact.
[08:37] Maya: On next bench deliverable — Arman will attach raw logs and a summary sheet. We also noted to test long-run stability for 4 hours.
[08:45] Arman: I'll schedule a 4-hour soak test hitting 1,200 tokens avg, with and without caching, and send the spreadsheet.
[08:55] Nina: For the SAML metadata — I'll send a bundle to Maya after this call.
[09:00] Maya: Great. Any blockers we didn't cover?
[09:04] Kevin: One minor — need clarity on who owns encryption-at-rest config for backups. Is that Redwood or Cobalt?
[09:12] Arman: For Redwood Private, backups are customer-managed when using CMK; we'll document the steps.
[09:20] Nina: Ok that helps.
[09:23] Maya: Let's do a quick recap and responsibilities.
[09:26] Maya: Maya to send security pack + SOC2 excerpts; Arman to run extended bench and share logs; Nina to provision SA and SAML metadata; Kevin to provide audit field list and retention; Diego to schedule canary and provide runbook skeleton.
[09:48] Dr. Mehra: One last ask — can you include a short note on model quantization impact on hallucination risk? Procurement asked about quality regressions with smaller models.
[09:59] Arman: We'll add a short section: quantization reduces numeric fidelity slightly; for instruction-tuned models we track quality regressions against eval prompts and can recommend thresholds.
[10:12] Maya: Perfect. Thanks all, we'll reconvene same day next week unless something urgent comes up.
[10:20] Nina: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional auto-transcription errors present (model names and product variants). Shared links: Security pack (link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/sec-pack/COBALT), Bench spreadsheet (https://redwood.ai/bench/COBALT-4591).
